skill.name: gjalla-code-review
skill.description: Review diffs and pull requests for merge readiness, prioritizing correctness, security, testing, maintainability, and user impact with location-specific fixes.
skill.summary: Assess code changes from relevant reviewer perspectives and return prioritized, actionable findings before merge.
skill.author: gjalla

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive: line 23 uses Markdown backticks to format `file:line` in prose. SKILL.md contains review guidance only, with no executable code, command invocation, or semantic threat identified.

static_findings.snippet: For each finding: `file:line`, what's wrong, and a concrete suggested fix. State what you verified a

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 23 uses backticks only as Markdown formatting around `file:line`. It contains no Ruby, shell command, or executable invocation.

content.value_statement: Code changes can hide correctness, security, and maintainability issues before merge. This skill reviews diffs from relevant perspectives and returns prioritized, location-specific fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews a complete diff against its intended behavior and available change context.
Assesses correctness, edge cases, testing, security, maintainability, and user impact.
Selects relevant engineering, product, quality, architecture, and security perspectives.
Groups findings as Blocking, Should fix, or Nit.
Provides a location, explanation, and concrete fix for each finding.
States what was verified and what could not be verified.
limitations: Requires the diff and enough context to understand the intended behavior.
Cannot inspect files, specifications, tests, or runtime behavior that are not provided.
Does not guarantee that every defect or security vulnerability will be identified.
Cannot replace test execution, specialist audits, or final human approval.

use_cases.title: Review Before Opening a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find blocking defects and missing tests before requesting review from teammates.

use_cases.title: Assess Merge Readiness
use_cases.description: Prioritize actionable findings and decide whether a pull request is ready to merge.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Product and Quality Impact
use_cases.description: Examine user impact, acceptance criteria, failure modes, and maintainability across a proposed change.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Diff Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff for merge readiness. Group findings as Blocking, Should fix, or Nit. Include location, problem, fix, and verification limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a small change with straightforward intent.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request against its description and acceptance criteria. Focus on correctness, edge cases, tests, and maintainability. Prioritize actionable findings with locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before requesting or granting approval.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Functional Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change from engineering, product, quality, and security perspectives where relevant. Identify second-order effects and missing handling. Explain merge risk and fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for changes that affect users, workflows, or sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Adversarial Ship-Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform an adversarial ship-readiness review of this diff and linked specification. Trace data access, failure modes, compatibility, and user impact. Report only defensible findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex or high-risk changes before production release.

output_examples.input: Review a change that adds payment retry behavior after request timeouts.
output_examples.output: Blocking — [changed file]:[line]. The retry path can submit a payment twice after a timeout. Add idempotency and test timeout recovery. Not verified: integration tests.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that introduces a shared cache for user preferences.
output_examples.output: Should fix — [changed file]:[line]. The cache key does not include the user identifier, so preferences can cross accounts. Scope keys per user and add isolation tests.

output_examples.input: Review a focused documentation-only naming correction.
output_examples.output: No Blocking or Should fix findings. The updated term is consistent throughout the provided diff. Not verified: references outside the supplied files.

best_practices: Provide the full diff, change intent, acceptance criteria, and relevant specifications.
Include test results and known constraints so findings can distinguish verified behavior from assumptions.
Resolve Blocking findings first, then evaluate Should fix items within the release context.
anti_patterns: Do not request approval from a partial diff that omits related changes.
Do not treat automated review as a substitute for tests or accountable human review.
Do not dismiss findings without checking the cited location, impact, and suggested fix.

faq.question: What changes can this skill review?
faq.answer: It can review diffs and pull requests when the changed code and intended behavior are available.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Findings are grouped as Blocking, Should fix, or Nit according to merge risk and practical impact.

faq.question: Does it review security concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. It examines data access, privacy, vulnerabilities, failure modes, and other security implications relevant to the change.

faq.question: Can it approve a pull request automatically?
faq.answer: It can assess readiness, but final approval remains with the responsible reviewer and team.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It can evaluate provided tests and results, but it does not guarantee runtime verification.

faq.question: What context produces the best review?
faq.answer: Provide the full diff, pull request description, acceptance criteria, linked specifications, test results, and known constraints.
